blind_spots_patched: Baseline Ch 5 framed 2025's >$1B Florida policyholder credits as voluntary tort-reform goodwill, missing Florida's statutory three-accident-year excess-profit limit that forced $1.2B of credits, plus Q3 2026 tariff and +16% PIP severity risks.

Baseline Ch 3 underestimated ad-cost inflation ($4,003M FY24; $5,133M FY25; $1.6B Q3 2026), overlooked Q3 2026 personal auto PLE falling 9% YoY and Oct Direct Auto CR breaching 96.1%, and missed that auto lines carry zero cat reinsurance.

Baseline Ch 6 missed the 2026 portfolio shift from U.S. Treasuries (54.3% to 41.9%) into Corporate/ABS/CMBS/RMBS (47.2%), $(2,432)M unrealized losses, Note 9 certified class actions, and had a 1-row shift in its 10-yr equity/investments table.

Baseline Ch 1 stated Progressive avoids share buybacks and relies purely on fixed + variable dividends, missing the 2026 pivot to $1.6B+ share repurchases (largest in 20+ years) funded alongside $1.5B of new Senior Notes.

Baseline Ch 2 did not quantify Progressive's heavy two-state geographic concentration in Texas and Florida (24.7% of FY2025 NPW) or TNC direct-enterprise vs. 90% agency commercial auto channel concentration.

Baseline Ch 4 did not capture the 2026 soft-market inflection where mutual/direct rivals resumed price cuts (turning personal auto market growth slightly negative) nor the ~104% H1 2026 commercial auto industry combined ratio gap.
assumptions_changed: WEAKENED: Progressive returns excess cash solely via a $0.10 quarterly fixed dividend and an annual variable dividend ($4.60 in Jan 2025; $13.50 in Jan 2026) while avoiding share buybacks and keeping debt minimal.
WEAKENED: Progressive runs 730-860 bps below its 96% combined ratio ceiling with ~$3.5B ad spend in 2024 and sustained Direct Auto momentum.
WEAKENED: Commercial Lines generates stable ~13.0% underwriting margins and higher retention to anchor Personal Lines.
CONFIRMED: Property (ASI) de-risked coastal exposure and maintains $75M Florida / $200M-$300M non-Florida cat retention under a ~$2.1B-$2.2B reinsurance tower.
CONFIRMED: Progressive maintains conservative Note 6 reserve triangles, strong cash conversion, and a high-grade bond portfolio.
